summary:
ASTRA-TWIN is an adaptive, predictive, recovery aware astronaut digital twin which seeks to advance astronaut health research with personalized monitoring, predictive analytics, and a digital representation of physiological changes during space missions. Although it goes beyond individual sensor readings and instead focuses on creating a more comprehensive view of an astronaut’s health and physiological status throughout a space mission by integrating data from multiple sources, including NASA research datasets.
Depending on the data available, ASTRA-TWIN aims to include a variety of vital-sign measurements (e.g., heart rate, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, body temperature) and, when appropriate, additional contextual data such as activity levels and environmental conditions.
Central to the project is the development of an adaptive personal baseline that captures each astronaut’s typical physiologic patterns and detects meaningful deviations.
Using artificial intelligence and data analysis techniques, the project seeks to identify relevant patterns and trends in vital-sign data and predict future changes.
Recovery prediction is another key goal, whereby pre-, during-, and post-activity vital-sign measurements are used to model post-exertion recovery trajectories and estimate the time required for key metrics to return to an individual’s personal baseline range.
details:
ASTRA-TWIN is a twin solution for astronauts, incorporating AI to monitor and predict an astronauts physical changes by combining medical data, environmental factors, physical activity and AI.

Traditional monitoring systems are focused on providing numerical data. ASTRA-TWIN aims to create a digital twin of the astronaut. This continuously learns about their own physiological parameters, identifies unusual changes, predicts potential future trends and monitors their recovery.

How Does the Project Work?

ASTRA-TWIN works with 5 key stages:

1. Data Collection & Monitoring

Collects physiological data (heart rate, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), breathing rate, body temperature and movement). If available it will also collect environmental data (temperature, humidity, CO₂ level and radiation).

2. Data Processing & Integration

Data will be cleaned, integrated and validated. Physiological, activity and environmental data will be combined to create an overall representation of the astronaut.

3. Adaptive Personal Baseline

Rather than using general parameters, ASTRA-TWIN aims to create a personal baseline for each astronaut. This is done by analysing the data and patterns of the astronaut. This means ASTRA-TWIN can understand what is typical for the astronaut and identify any anomalies.

4. AI-Based Prediction & Analysis

AI techniques and Machine Learning will be used to identify trends, find anomalies and predict potential future changes. There is also a what-if simulation so the astronaut can compare different scenarios of work, effort and recovery.

5. Recovery Prediction

An element of ASTRA-TWIN is the recovery-aware module. ASTRA-TWIN monitors physiological data before, during and after physical activity. This helps ASTRA-TWIN understand how the astronaut recovers. ASTRA-TWIN aims to predict the recovery path. This will predict how long it will take to get back to desired parameters within the personal range.

ASTRA-TWIN also considers how reliable the sensors are and how confident it is with its predictions.

Main Benefits

By using ASTRA-TWIN you can achieve:

Personalised monitoring of physiological data.

Identify anomalies early.

Predict desired physiological trends.

Better understanding of how each astronaut is recovering.

Combine physiological data with environmental data from the cabin.

Better interpretation of sensor data by validating and predicting confidence.

Interactive visualisations showing the current state of the astronaut and predicted trends.

Impact

ASTRA-TWIN aims to make human spaceflight safer and more intelligent by moving away from monitoring astronauts to personal intelligent analysis.

ASTRA-TWIN aims to help understand how astronauts respond to space environments, how their physiological states change throughout different mission activities and how their bodies recover.

This could also be useful for any application requiring continuous monitoring of physiological states, personal physiological analysis and recovery research.

ASTRA-TWIN is intended to be a research tool to support decisions, it is not intended to replace doctors or proven medical systems on board spacecraft.

Technologies Used

The intended prototype combines hardware, physiological sensors, data processing, AI and real-time visualisations.

Hardware:

ESP32 Microcontroller – Communicate with sensors and collect data.

MAX30102 Sensor – Pulse related measurements. Approximate blood oxygen saturation.

MPU6050 – Gyroscope to monitor movement/activity.

Appropriate Temperature Sensors.

Environmental Sensors – Humidity, CO₂ etc depending on the prototype setup.

Software & Development:

Python – Data processing, analysis and AI development.

Machine Learning – Scikit-learn, TensorFlow etc depending on model selection.

Data Visualisation – To visualise data, trends and predictions.

Embedded – To integrate ESP32 sensors.

Digital Dashboard – To display information relating to the astronauts and digital twin.

Data Sources:

NASA research resources, NASA Life Sciences Portal, Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) Environmental Data Application and relevant human space flight research investigations can provide background research and appropriate data sets.

Creativity & Innovation

The main innovation of ASTRA-TWIN is combining everything into a single personal digital twin. Key features include:

Adaptive Personal Baseline – Learns patterns of individuals and compares against their own parameters.

Multi-System Data Fusion – Combines data, physical activity data and environmental data for contextual analysis.

Intelligent – Uses AI to analyse trends and predict potential future physiological changes.

Recovery-Aware Intelligent – Analyses how desired physiological parameters change after activity and predicts individual recovery paths.

Confidence Aware AI – Considers sensor data quality and uncertainty with predictions to differentiate outputs.

What-If Simulation – Aims to compare different scenarios of mission activity and recovery.

These features mean ASTRA-TWIN is not just a monitoring tool. It is designed to be an evolving personalised predictive twin representing each astronaut.

Considerations

Differences – Each astronaut may have unique physiological patterns so personalisation is essential.

Sensor Accuracy – Data can be noisy and inaccurate so data needs to be validated.

Environmental Factors – Physiological data may be affected by spaceflight.

Data Integration – Data from various sensors needs to be synchronised.

Prediction Reliability – AI outputs need to consider uncertainty and be validated appropriately.

Recovery – Different physiological variables may recover at different rates so individual analysis is important.

Privacy – Personal physiological data should be treated responsibly.

Implementation – System must be implemented with readily available hardware/software and allow for expansion in the future.

Expected Outcome

The outcome of the project will be a functioning ASTRA-TWIN prototype. This will include a physiological and environmental data collection system, data processing, personal AI analysis modules, recovery prediction and interactive digital twin dashboard.

The prototype will demonstrate how sensor data and relevant NASA research data can be integrated to create a system which can be used to understand, analyse and predict astronaut physiological responses.

Ultimately we hope to move from monitoring what is happening to understanding what is changing, what could happen and how they are recovering.
